(iii)direct the Respondent to notify the elephant corridor in Chhattisgarh;
(iv)direct the respondents to create a Elephant Task Force in the State.
Further prayers are being made to call for protection, and safety of elephants in view of human-elephant conflict, to notify the elephant corridor and also to create a Task Force in the State.

3. Learned counsel for the State submits that the Forest Department, Government of Chhattisgarh has taken various measures to mitigate the human-elephant conflict and also ensures that the elephants have a good natural habitat with sufficient sources of food and water.
It is submitted that Government of Chhattisgarh and its Forest Department is committed to protecting the wildlife and management of the elephants as well.
Pursuant to order dated 12.03.2019, effective steps have been taken by Wppil 61 of 2020 the respondent authorities to ensure the safety of elephants.
To lessen the problem of human-elephant conflict, Forest Department is taking various initiatives to educate the masses as to how to deal with wild elephants.
A program called "Hamar Hathi Hamar Goth" is being broadcast from All India Radio Ambikapur Station to enable the villagers to exercise caution while moving in the areas.
In addition to this, Radio callers are installed on the elephants for recording their movements, so that preventive measures are being taken before the elephants enter the villages.

"SAJAG" App has been introduced, which is an App based Elephant Alert System,
IoT(Internet of Things) device to generate sound alert in villages using internet.
Every endeavour is being made to protect and preserve the elephants in accordance with law.

It is further categorically submitted by the State that Wildlife Institute of India (WII), Dehradun and the State have jointly initiated the project named "Conservation, Management of Elephants in Chhattisgarh: Capacity Dr. Anoop Bhalla (Ifs)(Retd) vs Union Of India on 25 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27585897/
2 Building Initiative On the Dispersal and Ranging Patterns for Effective Management of Human Elephant Interaction".

sentences.text: This project was initiated in the year 2017 for suggesting various measures for conservation and protection of elephants and to reduce elephant-human conflicts.
Sincere steps are being initiated by the State to reduce human-elephant conflicts and to provide better management and conservation methods for not only the elephants but also other wild animals.
Lastly, learned counsel submits that petitioners' reliefs have been adequately redressed/executed by the respondent/State authorities, as detailed in their reply dated 20.10.2020.
Wppil 61 of 2020 4.

Learned counsel for respondents-6 and 7 fairly submits that various reliefs prayed for by the petitioners have been adequately redressed and answered by these respondents, as detailed in their reply dated 10.01.2021.

It is submitted that CSPDCL (Chhattisgarh State Power Distribution Company Limited) is working strictly as per the standards prescribed in the Regulation 58 of the Central Electricity Authority (Measure relating to Safety and Electric Supply )Regulations, 2010.

entities.text: CSPDCL (Chhattisgarh State Power Distribution Company Limited)
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: It never flouted the prescription of standards/height/clearance for erecting electrical lines.
CSPDCL being concerned with the human-elephant conflict in the State, has been working rather rigorously in conforming to the directions issued by this Hon'ble Court order dated 12.03.2019.
Regular inspections of electricity connections are being conducted in the affected areas and instituted theft cases.

5. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the material available on record.
6.
Present petition is an off-shoot of the earlier WPPIL-5 of 2018 decided on 12.03.2019.

It appears that though significant number of deaths have happened due to electrification due to illegal electrical fencing which are put up by the inhabitants of certain villages in the year 2020, but appropriate legal actions have also been taken, in addition to generating awareness amongst people as no one support or grant liberty to any person for such illegal act.

Though steps taken by the State in relation to the open and naked transmission lines in certain areas, where movement of elephants has been noticed and established, but that by itself is not the complete answer to the problem.
Ways and means will Wppil 61 of 2020 have to be found so that the elephants are allowed to live in the forest, their natural habitat and minimum human contact between them is allowed to take place.

7. Some of the steps that have been taken by the respondent authorities are expected to yield results but it may not be the final solution as much more would be required to be done by deeper study by experts, who should be encouraged to provide their inputs on actual study basis, instead of out of the hat thinking, which may prove to be detrimental in the long run.
8. Present petition stands disposed of with liberty to the petitioner to assist the agencies involved in resolving the problem for which this petition was filed.
9. Disposal of the petition does not mean that the respondent authorities will go into hibernation.
Good work initiated and followed up by them should be carried on, if not for themselves, at least for the next generation.
